response:
Reflection: the frontier is now sharply defined. Dual cheapness (earnings yield plus capacity-to-price) with an own-norm capex-rate deviation delivers 4.5–4.6% alpha, and the single best refinement discovered last round was *two-year smoothing of the signed deviation* (t 4.82, the archive maximum, Sharpe 0.544) — durability of the spending stance matters more than the latest annual print. Two ingredients did not combine as hoped: volatility standardization degraded alpha once the norm was lagged (3.5%), and revenue-scaled capex raised the cross-sectional slope but lowered alpha, suggesting revenue scaling injects demand-cycle variation that FF5 partly prices. Abnormal capacity growth remains the weak form of the discipline leg. Accordingly this batch spends three slots consolidating persistence and benchmark timing plus valuation breadth, and two slots on genuinely new measurement of the investment leg: growth capex net of maintenance needs, and total real investment including inventory build folded into one measure rather than stacked as a second leg (stacking legs has failed twice).

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Dual cheapness persistent past-norm surprise
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ppent, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), NEG(MA(SUB(RATIO(capx, ppegt), MA(LAG(RATIO(capx, ppegt), 1), 4)), 2)))
HYPOTHESIS: The strongest disciplined-allocator profile combines cheapness on both earnings and installed capacity with a spending stance that has been below the firm's previously established capital policy for two consecutive years, so an uncontaminated benchmark and a durable deviation should reinforce each other.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The strictly-past four-year norm produced the largest single-cheapness alpha (4.9%) and two-year smoothing produced the most reliable alpha t-statistic (4.82); both act on the deviation and neither has been tested with the other. If the two gains are additive this becomes the archive leader on both magnitude and reliability.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Dual cheapness three-year stance deviation
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ppent, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), NEG(MA(SUB(RATIO(capx, ppegt), MA(RATIO(capx, ppegt), 5)), 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: If mispricing arises from slow market recognition of a changed capital-allocation regime, then averaging the deviation over three years should capture the regime even better than two, up to the point where staleness dominates and the signal decays.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Two-year smoothing improved reliability over the unsmoothed deviation, and this locates the optimum of the persistence horizon rather than assuming it; a decline at three years would show the effect is a medium-horizon expectation error, while a further improvement would push the final signal toward very low turnover. Either outcome directly informs which construction to submit in the final generations.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Triple cheapness persistent capex restraint
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ppent, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho))))), NEG(MA(SUB(RATIO(capx, ppegt), MA(RATIO(capx, ppegt), 5)), 2)))
HYPOTHESIS: Price expectations are best measured against several fundamental anchors at once — profit, installed capacity, and revenue scale — because each is contaminated by different accounting noise, and a firm cheap on all three while restraining spending is the clearest disciplined-allocator case.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Broadening cheapness from one to two channels was the single largest improvement in the archive (t 4.52 from 4.09), so the marginal value of a third, revenue-based anchor is the natural next test while the discipline leg is held at its best-performing smoothed form. The nesting keeps the valuation composite and the discipline leg equally weighted so the comparison is clean.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Cheap with capex near maintenance need
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ppent, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), NEG(RATIO(SUB(capx, DELTA(SUB(ppegt, ppent), 1)), ppegt)))
HYPOTHESIS: Only capital spending in excess of what is needed to replace worn-out capacity represents a discretionary growth bet; measuring capex net of the year's accumulated-depreciation increase separates genuine expansion from unavoidable maintenance, and cheap firms spending near maintenance level are the disciplined allocators.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: All discipline measures so far benchmark spending against the firm's own past behavior, which cannot distinguish a firm that habitually overspends from one that simply owns short-lived assets; the gross-minus-net PPE change gives a direct, contemporaneous estimate of required replacement investment. This is an absolute economic benchmark rather than a statistical one, so it could add information orthogonal to the own-norm deviation.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Gross capacity cheapness with persistent restraint
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ppegt, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), NEG(MA(SUB(RATIO(capx, ppegt), MA(RATIO(capx, ppegt), 5)), 2)))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheapness relative to physical capacity should be measured on a gross rather than net basis, because gross plant approximates the replacement cost of the productive base while net plant reflects accumulated depreciation choices that vary with asset age and accounting policy.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The capacity-to-price leg was the key valuation innovation, but its net-PPE construction mechanically favors firms with old, heavily depreciated assets, which may be a value trap rather than a cheapness signal. Swapping to gross plant isolates that one measurement choice while keeping the best discipline leg fixed.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Cheap with total real investment restraint
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ppent, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), NEG(MA(SUB(RATIO(ADD(capx, DELTA(invt, 1)), ppegt), MA(RATIO(ADD(capx, DELTA(invt, 1)), ppegt), 5)), 2)))
HYPOTHESIS: Real investment is fixed capital plus the change in inventory, and a disciplined firm restrains both; embedding inventory investment inside a single own-norm deviation should capture total resource commitment better than either channel alone.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Inventory discipline independently produced positive alpha (2.7–2.9%) but stacking it as a separate rank leg diluted the composite, implying the problem was aggregation, not economics. Summing the two flows before benchmarking them against the firm's own norm keeps a single, well-scaled discipline measure and tests whether working-capital commitment adds information to physical capex.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
